newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar trade sees higher outstation buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar trade sees higher outstation buying.

text.p: Indian sugar prices on Friday bounced back from lower levels while higher outstation buying was seen in southern and central Indian markets, dealers said.
Renewed consumer buying as well as fresh enquiries from retailers lifted prices. Arrivals were at low ebb.
Ready delivery sugar S-30 rose by 5/25 rupees to 1,250/1,295 rupees per quintal while sugar M-30 rose by 10 rupees to 1,280/1,360 rupees per quintal.
Sugar mill delivery was steady at 1,190/1,200 rupees per quintal. Overall volumes remained low during the day and traders said they were expecting narrow price movements next week.
